name: חֲצַרְמָוֶת
gloss: settlement of death; the land Hadramawt
summary: A son of Joktan, of the line of Shem through Eber, whose name is that of a people and land in southern Arabia, among Joktan’s other sons Sheba, Ophir and Havilah. As the Hebrew writes it, it is חֲצַר “settlement” joined to מָוֶת “death”. The Sabaic inscriptions name the land ḥḍrmwt, Hadramawt, with ḍ: that is the “settlement, dwelling” root of Arabic ḥaḍar and Sabaic ḥḍr, not the “enclosure” root. Whether its second part meant “death” to those who named it is not shown.

evidence.note: Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, חֲצַרְמָוֶת and Jerah.
The root’s noun of Arabian peoples: Ishmael’s sons “by their חֲצֵרִים”, their settlements.

evidence.locator: p. 185, ḤḌR II (nisba “Hadramis”, from n.loc. ḤḌRM(W)T); p. 277, MLK (Ir 32/9, ḥḍrmwt)

note: Biella read from OCR text only. The Sabaic spelling ḥḍrmwt matches מָוֶת in its consonants; no Sabaic text found here explains the second element.
